Surah "Al-Duha" (The Morning Brightness)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the morning brightness﴾. The intended meaning is the time of forenoon (al-duha), which is the early part of the day, when the sun rises. The reason the time of forenoon was singled out for the oath is that it is the hour in which Musa (peace be upon him) was addressed, and in which the sorcerers were thrown down prostrate. Or it means the entire day, as it is contrasted with the night in His saying:

By the night when it becomes still (﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى﴾), [al-Nasafi says]: "sakan" (it became still, calm). What is meant is the stillness of people and of sounds within it. And the answer to the oath (جواب القسم) is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 3:

﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He come to hate you.﴾ He has not abandoned you since He chose you, and He has not come to hate you since He loved you. The word tawdi‘ (taking leave, forsaking) is an intensive form of wad‘ (leaving), because one who takes leave of you in separation has gone to the utmost extent in leaving you. It is narrated that "revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for some days, so the polytheists said: Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him and come to hate him. Then this was revealed."

The omission of the pronoun from qala (وقلى, "and hated"), like its omission from al-dhakirat (الذاكرات) in His saying: ﴿And the men and women who remember Allah much﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35], meaning: wa-l-dhakirati-hi (and the women who remember Him), and similarly fa-awa (فآوى, "and sheltered"), fa-hada (فهدى, "and guided"), fa-aghna (فأغنى, "and enriched"), is a verbal abbreviation (ikhtisar lafzi, a shortening of the wording), because the omitted element is evident.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 93, verse 4:

﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first.﴾ That is: what Allah has prepared for you in the Hereafter, of the *maqam mahmud* (the praiseworthy station), the *hawd mawrud* (the Pool that is reached), and the promised good, is better than what pleased you in this world. (p-٦٥٤) It was also said: the connection of this verse with what precedes it is that, since it contained the negation of farewell and of abandonment, namely that Allah is continuing to join you with revelation and that you are the beloved of Allah, and you see no honour greater than that, He informed him that his state in the Hereafter is greater than that, because of his precedence over the prophets, the testimony of his community over the nations, and other things besides.

**﴿And your Lord will surely give you﴾**, in the Hereafter, of reward and the station of intercession, and other things,

**﴿so that you will be well-pleased﴾**. When this was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then I will never be pleased while a single one of my community is in the Fire."

The lam that enters upon *sawfa* is the lam of inception (*lam al-ibtida'*), which emphasizes the content of the sentence, and a subject has been omitted. Its estimated form is: "And you, your Lord will surely give you." A similar case is *la-uqsimu* ("I swear"), according to the reading of one who reads it that way, since the meaning is "Indeed, I swear." This is because if it were the lam of oath (*lam al-qasam*), its lam would not enter upon the present-tense verb except with the emphatic nun (*nun al-tawkid*). Therefore it must be the lam of inception, and this lam only enters upon a subject (*mubtada'*) or a predicate (*khabar*), so an estimated subject and predicate must be assumed, as we have mentioned. This is what the author of *al-Kashshaf* mentioned. But the author of *al-Kashshaf* also said: it is the lam of oath, and the emphatic nun was dispensed with, because the nun is only added to indicate that the lam is the lam of oath and not the lam of inception. It is known that it is not the lam of inception, because it enters upon *sawfa*, and the lam of inception does not enter upon *sawfa*. He also mentioned that the combination of the two particles of emphasis and delay indicates that the giving is certain to occur, though delayed. Then He enumerated to him His blessings from the beginning of his condition, so that the one who awaits the grace of Allah may measure it against what has already passed from Him, lest he expect anything but the best and increase in goodness, and lest his chest be constricted or his patience diminish. So He said:

Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?

Here the verb "yajidka" (يَجِدْكَ, "find you") is of the type that means "to know" (min al-wujud alladhi bi-ma'na al-'ilm), and the two accusatives after it are its two objects. The meaning is: "Were you not an orphan when your parents died,

﴿فَآوى﴾ meaning: He sheltered you with your uncle Abu Talib, and he took you into his care until he sponsored you and raised you?!"

Verse 7: "And He found you lost (ḍāll), and guided you."

Al-Nasafi's commentary (Madarik al-Tanzil) on this verse: "(And He found you lost) meaning: not knowing, and not acquainted with the landmarks of prophethood (nubuwwah) and the rulings of the sharia (sharīʿah), and those matters whose path is revelation (samʿ) (p-655). (And He guided you), so He made you aware of the sharia and the Qur'an?! It has also been said: he went astray on the road to Syria when Abu Talib took him out, and He returned him to the caravan. It is not permissible to understand by it a deviation from the truth or falling into error, for from the beginning of his state until the revelation descended upon him, he (ﷺ) was protected (maʿṣūm) from the worship of idols and the filth of the people of wickedness and disobedience."

Notes on terms: ḍāll (lost, astray); nubuwwah (prophethood); sharīʿah (the sacred law); samʿ (transmitted revelation, as opposed to reason); maʿṣūm (protected from sin).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 8:**

﴿And He found you poor⁠ — ﴾ "poor" (faqīran),

﴿and enriched you﴾: He enriched you with the wealth of Khadijah, or with what He bestowed upon you from the spoils of war?!

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 9:

﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him.﴾ Do not overpower him regarding his wealth and his right, because of his weakness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 10:

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not repel him.﴾ That is, do not rebuke him. Give something small, or return a kind word. And from al-Suddi: what is meant is the seeker of knowledge, when he comes to you; do not rebuke him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 11:

﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, speak of it.﴾ That is: speak of the prophethood which Allah has given you, and it is the greatest of favours. The sound view is that it encompasses all of Allah's favours upon him, and included within it is the teaching of the Qur'an and the sacred laws (shara'i', sing. shari'a, the revealed legal prescriptions).
